content.thinking:
I'm weighing whether the placeholder already carries the "at least" wording, since the figures say "at least 9m 19s" and I can't tell if {duration} includes that phrase. Saying "lasted at least {duration}" would be the safer way to keep the meaning either way.

I'm settling on the placeholder wording: the value already seems to carry "at least," so I'll use "lasted {duration}" without adding it again. For the cost, I'll say the loss was an estimated {customer_loss}, and that nobody was paged. The setting hasn't been undone, since that was left to a person, and a draft fix is open as PR #540 but not applied, so I won't call it resolved. For who was affected, I'll say "some shoppers" and keep the likely-cause clause as a hedge.

input.overview: For {duration}, account pages on io-shop failed for some shoppers, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. It started when a setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages was switched on. No record that Argus read shows who or what switched it on. The summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. No one was paged, so no on-call responders were called in. Argus did not undo the suspected change because that change is missing from the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person. Argus also opened a proposed fix, PR #540, as a draft. The fix has not been applied.
